digest.component_or_area: plan-review severity grading and impact model
propositions: The 'undecomposed' axis fires on 0.107% of plan-v3 verified findings (11/10,250) and 0.153% of plan-v4 (18/11,773), two orders of magnitude below other severity axes, while holding hard-override power that floors impact to 0.85

The cited G5 deterministic suppressor that justifies the low fire rate is inert in practice: the 'g5_undecomposed_vetoed' coverage key appears zero times across 2,000 reviews, and 90%+ of reviewed tickets are childless so the suppressor cannot apply

The hard-override floor of 0.85 is miscalibrated: it treats all non-none grades equally, so 16 of 29 fires were graded 'low' but floored to impact 0.85, and in 25 of 29 fires the undecomposed axis was the sole override producing a block decision

The inverse population—findings whose text matches the flat-plan regex but scored 'undecomposed=none'—shows 33 plan-v3 and 17 plan-v4 matches, but sampling shows these are regex false positives about code decomposition, not missed flat-plan defects

The 29 genuine fires were found to be valid flat-plan findings (bundled independently-releasable slices and one store-grounded child-count mismatch), confirming the axis detects real defects but is miscalibrated in its floor behavior, matching the pre-fix state of 'ac_unverifiable' and 'divergent_implementation'

The axis prompt text's suppressor justification contradicts observational evidence: the suppressor never fired, is inapplicable to childless tickets, yet the text claims it explains the low rate; the axis text must be rewritten and the floor behavior retargeted before impact-model-version bump
